title: RAW_UNSCREENED: medizinischer Glossar- versus Rezeptregister
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: period caches show learned drug/part names beside qualities in glossaries and separate measures/actions in recipes; HERB4 may switch register within a shared form inventory.

design.scope_description: HERB4 complete lines f17r.5, f21r.12 and f29v.1 plus historical comparison documented in GDT625/GDT809.
design.mechanism: A register switch uses the same whole-form vocabulary for descriptive materia entries and prescriptive recipe fields, with explicit local record type.
design.unit: The three exact lines and their neighboring part/quality/value forms.
design.contrast: Descriptive glossary register versus executable recipe register.
design.prediction: Glossary reading predicts head→part/quality→degree layouts and no required temporal output; recipe reading predicts material→amount/action→result layouts with written operands.
concrete_observations: f17r.5 cthy chor shor contains several part-like wholes without a written amount token in the local span.
f21r.12 chor chol daiin and f29v.1 ... cthy ... daiin place part-like forms near value-like fields.
linked_consequences: A glossary register should preserve parallel descriptive fields even when no operation is present.
A recipe register should require a written action/result pair before treating a value as a prescription.
design.nearest_rival: One uniform recipe or one uniform descriptive genre across all four paragraphs.
design.distinguishing_observation: Classify each complete line by written operand/result obligations, then test whether the same whole-form value remains stable within each register; mixed genre is supported only by recurring formal switch cues.
assumption_costs: historical register analogues transfer only structurally
line grouping is inherited from exposed source
design.strongest_likely_failure: The same 145 groups can be made coherent under both genres because no independent genre marker is decoded.
